# Prioritize rubrics

## Priority (the value judgement: how much the issue fixes or unblocks)

| Priority | Meaning |
|---|---|
| P0 | Fixes something broken, or other queued issues are blocked by it |
| P1 | Normal planned work |
| P2 | Nice to have, nobody waits for it |

## Size and Estimate

Judge the size against the code you looked at, not only the issue text.

| Size | Effort | Estimate (hours) |
|---|---|---|
| XS | under 1 hour | 1 |
| S | up to half a day | 3 |
| M | about a day | 6 |
| L | 2-3 days | 16 |
| XL | more | split it, do not queue |

## Understanding the code (step 2 checklist)

- Is the behaviour already there, fully or partly? Then say so; do not queue duplicate work.
- Which modules, scripts or skills would it change? Name them, without file paths in comments that go stale.
- Does it use something another queued issue creates (an interface, a script, a file format)? Then it depends on that issue.
- Do two issues change the same code? Queue them one after the other, the more fundamental first, to avoid merge conflicts.
- Is a listed blocker no longer needed (the thing it provides already exists, or the dependency was only an assumption)?

## Comment on every issue you ranked or left

```markdown
> *This was generated by AI during triage.*
Queue position: #k of N
Priority P1: <reason>. Size M (~6h): <reason, based on the code>.
Blockers: #x (Done), #y (ranked #j in this run) | none
Relationships changed: added #y (<why>) | removed #z (<why>) | none
```

For an issue left in Triage replace the position by `Not queued:` and the reason. Add `(no board, nothing moved)` when there is no board.

## Commands

```bash
gh issue comment <n> --body-file - <<'COMMENT'
> *This was generated by AI during triage.*
Queue position: #1 of 3
...
COMMENT
gh label create needs-info --force      # once, if the label does not exist (name per the repo's label mapping)
gh issue edit <n> --add-label needs-info
```
